prompt.context_jp: 某国大使館の地下駐車場___、消火装置の誤作動によって噴き出した二酸化炭素で、じわじわと満たされつつあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 某国大使館の地下駐車場___、...満たされつつあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames the parking lot as the setting the narrator will describe.

feedback.correct_en: は presents the parking lot as the known stage/topic that the sentence will say something about. The narrator is describing the state of that location.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as newly introduced new information, but this sentence is a scene-setting description of an already-named place. を doesn't fit an intransitive like 満たされつつあった.

contrast_examples.jp: 駐車場は満たされていた。
contrast_examples.en: The parking lot (topic) was filling up.

contrast_examples.jp: 駐車場が満たされていた。
contrast_examples.en: It was the parking lot that was filling up (new focus).

prompt.context_jp: 「無線___通じない そっちは？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 無線___通じない
prompt.prompt_en: Kitami discovers the radio has just failed. Pick the particle that reports this as new information.

feedback.correct_en: が reports a fresh discovery — he's just realized the radio isn't working. New-information が fits an urgent on-the-spot observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 無線 as an established topic being contrasted with something else, which doesn't match this sudden exclamation.

contrast_examples.jp: 電気はつかないけど水は出る。
contrast_examples.en: The lights don't work, but water does. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 無線___届かず、外界との連絡はすでに絶たれている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 無線___届かず、...
prompt.prompt_en: Narration summarizing the situation. Choose the particle that treats the radio as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: This is calm narrator exposition, parallel with the following 連絡はすでに絶たれている. は presents each item as a topic for assessment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like a sudden on-the-spot discovery (as in line 7's dialogue), not a narrator's overview.

prompt.context_jp: そこへ、黒塗りの公用車から降り立った女性___いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ...降り立った女性___いた。
prompt.prompt_en: A new character is being introduced to the scene. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces a brand-new referent into the discourse — the woman has not been mentioned before. Existential ある/いる with a new subject takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that this woman is already known to the reader, which contradicts her first appearance here.

contrast_examples.jp: 昔々、おじいさんがいました。
contrast_examples.en: Long ago, there was an old man. (introducing)

contrast_examples.jp: そのおじいさんは山へ行きました。
contrast_examples.en: That old man went to the mountain. (already known)

prompt.context_jp: 時間だけ___無情に流れ、決断の刻限が迫っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時間だけ___無情に流れ、...
prompt.prompt_en: The sentence emphasizes that *only* time flows, nothing else moves. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: だけ + が highlights time as the one exhaustive thing that is moving while everything else is frozen. This exhaustive-focus pattern needs が.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would shift the nuance to 'as for only time (in contrast to something else)' — less natural here where time is being singled out as what moves.

prompt.context_jp: 顔色___急に失せ、額には脂汗が滲んでいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 顔色___急に失せ、...
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator notices a sudden change in Governor Akatsuka. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が reports an observed change happening right now. Physical state changes noticed in the moment (顔色が変わる, 汗が出る) typically take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 顔色 as a general topic being evaluated, losing the sense of sudden onset.

prompt.context_jp: そもそも応答___ないということは もう亡くなっている可能性が高い
prompt.prompt_jp: 応答___ないということは
prompt.prompt_en: Shirakane is reasoning in the abstract: 'the fact that there's no response means...'. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a こと/という nominalized clause describing a situation, the subject typically takes が. Here 応答がない forms a factual condition.
feedback.incorrect_en: 応答はない could stand alone as a topic-comment statement, but embedded in ...ないということは, が is natural for the inner subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 返事がないということは、断られたのだろう。
contrast_examples.en: The fact that there's no reply means we were turned down.

prompt.context_jp: その膠着を破ったの___、後方に控えていた目黒の通信だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その膠着を破ったの___、...目黒の通信だった。
prompt.prompt_en: A cleft sentence identifying exactly what broke the stalemate. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: ...のは Xだった is a cleft structure: the first part is the topic/presupposition, and X is the exhaustive answer. は marks that topic slot.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would make the clause itself a bare subject, but the sentence pattern here is 'The one who broke it = Meguro's call', which requires は.

contrast_examples.jp: 犯人を見つけたのは彼だ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who found the culprit is him.

prompt.context_jp: 重く閉ざされていたシャッター___不意に持ち上がり、外の光と冷たい空気が一気に流れ込む。
prompt.prompt_jp: ...シャッター___不意に持ち上がり、...
prompt.prompt_en: A dramatic, unexpected event in the scene. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が signals a sudden, eventive new happening — the shutter unexpectedly lifting. Narrative event clauses with 不意に strongly favor が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a calm description of the shutter's property, not a surprise event.

prompt.context_jp: 焦りだけ___積み重なり、誰の顔にも汗が浮かんでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 焦りだけ___積み重なり、...
prompt.prompt_en: Only impatience was piling up — nothing else happened. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: だけが emphasizes that impatience was the single thing accumulating, while progress stalled. Exhaustive focus takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would contrast 焦り against another topic, but here nothing else is being contrasted — only 焦り is singled out.

contrast_examples.en: At least the sound could be heard. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: その一歩で、現場の主導権___明らかに彼女の手へと移った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 現場の主導権___明らかに彼女の手へと移った。
prompt.prompt_en: Narration comments on what happened to the initiative. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 主導権 is treated as the topic being discussed — the narrator is telling us what became of it. は fits this topic-comment framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as newly introduced information, but 主導権 is already an understood element of this political scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 権力が動いた瞬間だった。
contrast_examples.en: It was the moment power moved. (event focus)

prompt.context_jp: 駒場の声___、押し殺した怒りで低く震えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 駒場の声___、低く震えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator describes a quality of Komaba's voice. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は presents 駒場の声 as the topic the narrator is characterizing. Descriptive statements about a known referent take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read like a sudden on-stage event discovery, clashing with the reflective descriptive tone.

prompt.context_jp: 地下駐車場___に 閉じ込められている
prompt.prompt_jp: 地下駐車場___ 閉じ込められている
prompt.prompt_en: 'Trapped inside the parking lot.' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 閉じ込められる takes に to mark the location where someone is confined/stuck — a resulting location, not an activity location.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the setting of an action, but 閉じ込められる focuses on being contained *at* a place. を doesn't fit this passive.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に閉じ込められた。
contrast_examples.en: I was locked in the room.
I studied in the room. (activity location)

prompt.context_jp: 警備員たちは警戒レベル___一段上げて門を固く閉ざしている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 警戒レベル___一段上げて
prompt.prompt_en: 'Raised the alert level by one notch.' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 上げる is transitive — the guards actively raise the alert level. The direct object takes を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 警戒レベル the subject (as if it rose on its own, which needs 上がる instead). に doesn't mark the thing being changed.

prompt.context_jp: 止めに入る喜多見の声を、千住___ひとことで遮った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 千住___ひとことで遮った。
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator describes what Senju did. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Senju is already an established character and the scene's topic here. は marks him as the agent being talked about.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would highlight Senju as the newly identified doer (exhaustive), but the context isn't asking 'who did it?' — it's describing his reaction.

prompt.context_jp: 場面___都心の美容室に移る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 場面は都心の美容室___移る。
prompt.prompt_en: 'The scene shifts TO a beauty salon.' Pick the particle for the destination.

feedback.correct_en: 移る takes に to mark the destination — the place something moves TO.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks a location of activity, not a destination. を would mark a path or object, not a goal.

prompt.context_jp: 大使館の敷地は日本の主権の___土地であり、いくら救助のためでも無断で立ち入って侵すことは許されない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 日本の主権の___土地
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the phrase that fits '[land where Japan's sovereignty does not extend]'.

feedback.correct_en: 主権が及ぶ is the set collocation meaning 'sovereignty extends/reaches'. The negative 及ばぬ fits a legal/political register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 届かぬ is used for physical signals or deliveries (無線が届かない), not for authority. 渡らぬ doesn't collocate with 主権 at all.

contrast_examples.en: An area beyond the reach of law.

prompt.context_jp: 押し問答は___し、駒場のもとには次々と厳しい報告だけが上がってくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 押し問答は___し、...
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning the argument became deadlocked / stuck.

feedback.correct_en: 膠着する means 'to become stuck in a deadlock' — perfect for an unresolved standoff.
feedback.incorrect_en: 衝突 means 'collision/clash' (an active impact, not stalling). 崩壊 means 'collapse', the opposite of a frozen stalemate.

prompt.context_jp: 大動脈遮断で 一時的に止血しましたが あくまで___です 根本手術しないと助かりません
prompt.prompt_jp: あくまで___です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the medical term meaning 'emergency/temporary stopgap treatment'.

feedback.correct_en: 応急処置 means emergency first-aid / stopgap measure — exactly the sense of 'temporarily stopped bleeding, not a cure'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 根本治療 is the opposite — fundamental/curative treatment (which is what he still needs). 予防措置 means preventive measures (before illness).

contrast_examples.jp: 根本的な治療が必要だ。

prompt.context_jp: 要救助者より 自分の命を___させたら レスキューじゃないんだよ！
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の命を___させたら
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'to put X first / prioritize X'.

feedback.correct_en: 優先させる = 'make X take priority'. Komaba is saying a rescuer who puts their own life first isn't a rescuer.
feedback.incorrect_en: 優越 means 'superiority' and doesn't take させる in this way. 優秀 is an adjective meaning 'excellent'.

prompt.context_jp: 大使の許可が___に近い形であったことに、彼女は納得していない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大使の許可が___に近い形
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the term for 'approval given AFTER the act was already done'.

feedback.correct_en: 事後承諾 = retroactive consent, approval granted after the fact. That's exactly what happened: MER broke in, then got permission.
feedback.incorrect_en: 事前承諾 means consent BEFORE acting — the opposite. 相互承諾 means mutual consent, which doesn't match a one-sided after-the-fact approval.

contrast_examples.jp: 事後承諾になってしまった。
contrast_examples.en: It ended up as retroactive approval.

prompt.context_jp: ネットの声っていうのは ___が好きですね
prompt.prompt_jp: ネットの声は ___ が好き
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'flipping one's opinion 180°'.

feedback.correct_en: 手のひら返し describes abruptly reversing one's attitude — exactly what the internet did (heroes → villains overnight).
feedback.incorrect_en: 腹の探り合い means 'feeling each other out' (probing). 目の付け所 means 'the point one notices / angle of attention'. Neither captures reversal.

contrast_examples.jp: 世論は手のひらを返した。
二人は腹の探り合いをしていた。
contrast_examples.en: The two were probing each other's intentions.

prompt.context_jp: あなた こんなとこで ___ような タマじゃないでしょ！
prompt.prompt_jp: こんなとこで ___ような タマじゃない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the rough/casual verb Kitami shouts at Senju meaning 'to die / kick the bucket'.

feedback.correct_en: くたばる is a blunt, almost rude verb for dying. It fits Kitami's desperate, shouting tone and matches the rough phrase タマじゃない.
feedback.incorrect_en: 亡くなる is polite/respectful — wrong register for yelling at a comrade not to die. お休みになる is honorific for sleeping.

contrast_examples.jp: こんなとこでくたばってたまるか。
祖父が亡くなりました。

prompt.context_jp: ガス爆発の現場で 部下を助けてもらった借りがある これで ___にしてもらうぞ
prompt.prompt_jp: これで ___にしてもらうぞ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the colloquial word meaning 'even / square (no more debt)'.

feedback.correct_en: チャラにする is a casual idiom meaning 'to call it even / wipe the slate clean' — fitting Senju's blunt tough-guy register.
feedback.incorrect_en: バラ and ハラ don't form idioms with にする in this sense. Only チャラ carries the 'cancel out a debt' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: Wipe out the debt / call it even.

prompt.prompt_en: Kitami inside the trapped parking lot has just picked up his radio and found it dead. Which line sounds most natural for that in-the-moment discovery?

choices.text: 無線が通じない。そっちは？
無線は通じない。そっちは？
無線を通じない。そっちは？

feedback.correct_en: At the moment of discovery, が naturally reports the newly observed fact. The story itself uses this form in line 7.
feedback.incorrect_en: B (は) would frame the radio as an established topic being contrasted — fine for narrator exposition (as in line 4) but off for a surprised in-the-moment utterance. C is ungrammatical: 通じる is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: Huh, the lights won't come on! (discovery, が)

contrast_examples.jp: この部屋は電気がつかない。
contrast_examples.en: In this room, the lights don't work. (topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 駒場 to Governor Akatsuka, asking her to come back after her illness.
prompt.prompt_en: Komaba is speaking respectfully to the governor who is seriously ill. Which line is most natural?

choices.text: ですから 必ず戻ってきてください。
だから 絶対 戻ってこいよ。
つきましては 戻ってこられますように。

feedback.correct_en: Polite but direct ですから…ください fits a trusted subordinate speaking from the heart to his superior — exactly the story's line.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is rough casual (戻ってこいよ), inappropriate for addressing the governor. C is overly formal/distant and uses 'may you be able to', weakening the plea.

contrast_examples.jp: 必ず戻ってきてください。

contrast_examples.en: You'd better come back! (rough, among peers)

prompt.context_jp: Komaba, angry, shouting at Minister Shirakane about what a rescuer is.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for this emotional outburst?

choices.text: 要救助者より 自分の命を優先させたら レスキューじゃないんだよ！
要救助者から 自分の命を優先させたら レスキューじゃないんだよ！
要救助者で 自分の命を優先させたら レスキューじゃないんだよ！

feedback.correct_en: より marks the standard of comparison — 'prioritize your own life over the victim'. This is the natural collocation with 優先させる.
feedback.incorrect_en: から would mean 'from the victim', which makes no sense. で marks location/means, also wrong here.

contrast_examples.jp: 家族より仕事を優先する。
安全より速度を優先する。

prompt.context_jp: Senju, recovering, tells Kitami he owes him. Kitami jokes back.
prompt.prompt_en: After Senju says この借りは必ずまた返す, which reply by Kitami fits the warm, teasing comrade tone?

choices.text: じゃ 今度 メシでもおごってください。
では 後日 お食事を奢っていただければ幸いです。

feedback.correct_en: メシでもおごってください is light, informal-polite banter — perfect for two colleagues who've just survived a crisis together. This matches the story's line.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is stiffly formal, as if to a client. C is too curt/rough to feel warm. The でも softens the request to 'something like a meal'.

contrast_examples.en: How about a coffee or something? (light offer)

contrast_examples.jp: コーヒーを飲ませてください。
contrast_examples.en: Please let me drink coffee. (unnaturally stiff)

prompt.context_jp: Senju, gasping in CO2, telling Kitami to run no matter what.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version of Senju's dying command sounds most natural for his tough-guy register?

choices.text: いいか 約束しろ 俺に何かあっても かまわず 全力で走れ。
いいですか 約束してください 私に何かあっても どうぞ 全力で走ってください。
ねえ 約束してね 僕に何かあっても 気にせず 走ろうね。

feedback.correct_en: Senju is a gruff rescue-squad leader. 俺・しろ・走れ imperatives match his blunt masculine speech and life-or-death urgency.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly polite — doesn't fit a desperate order between comrades. C is soft/childish (僕・ね・走ろうね), completely wrong for Senju's voice.
